verdicts.claim: By default SQLite auto-checkpoints on the COMMIT that makes the WAL 1000 pages or more (about 4 MB). It also checkpoints when the last connection closes
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection on a database file closes'; 'about 1000 pages (and is thus about 4MB'; SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT named

verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpoints are always PASSIVE. sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() is also PASSIVE, and PASSIVE is the default checkpoint style.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'The default checkpoint style is PASSIVE ... All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE.'

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE copies as many frames as it can without waiting for readers or writers. It can leave the checkpoint unfinished. It never invokes the busy handler
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode. On the other hand, passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished'

verdicts.claim: FULL ... While it is pending it blocks new writers, but not new readers.
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'This mode blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.'

verdicts.claim: Checkpoints are mutually exclusive across processes. If another process is already running a checkpoint, the call fails with SQLITE_BUSY, and the busy handler is not invoked
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'If any other process is running a checkpoint operation at the same time, the lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.'

verdicts.claim: pnLog/pnCkpt are -1 on error or when the database is not in WAL mode. After a successful TRUNCATE both are 0.
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: '*pnLog is set ... to -1 if the checkpoint could not run because of an error or because the database is not in WAL mode'; 'truncated to zero bytes and so both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero.'

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA journal_size_limit ... The default is -1 (no limit).
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'The default journal size limit is -1 (no limit).'

verdicts.claim: WAL-reset bug likely present 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09); fixed in 3.51.3 (2026-03-13); backports 3.44.6 and 3.50.7
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) ... Backports ... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7'; release log: 'Fix the WAL-reset database corruption bug.'

verdicts.claim: Dates differ: wal.html says bug found and fixed 2026-03-03; Canonical says SQLite disclosed and published the fix March 5, 2026
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'On 2026-03-03, one of the SQLite developers (Dan) found and fixed a bug'; Canonical: 'On March 5, 2026 SQLite disclosed the bug and published a fix.'

verdicts.claim: A forced TRUNCATE waits for all active readers and writers ... Litestream says this can block writes and readers for a long time when a long-lived read
verdicts.evidence: Litestream: 'A forced TRUNCATE checkpoint ... waits for both all active readers AND writers to complete before truncating the WAL. Long-lived read transactions will cause extended blocking periods.'
